title: SQS & SNS: Queues, Fan-out and Decoupling
summary: Buffer work with SQS, broadcast with SNS, and combine them for fan-out.
tldr: **SQS** is a pull-based buffer: producers keep working when consumers are slow or down, and workers scale on queue depth. Each message is handled by **one** consumer and deleted after processing.

**SNS** pushes each message to **every** subscriber. **SNS → one SQS queue per consumer** is the classic fan-out: each service gets a copy, works at its own pace and can go offline without losing events.
Several apps must **re-read the same ordered stream** in real time? That's **Kinesis Data Streams**, not SQS. Content-based routing of AWS, SaaS or custom events? **EventBridge**.
Migrating an app that speaks **JMS, AMQP, MQTT or OpenWire** without code changes? Use **Amazon MQ** (ActiveMQ or RabbitMQ), not SQS.

keyFacts.text: Default and maximum **visibility timeout**. For a Lambda consumer, AWS recommends a visibility timeout of at least **6×** the function timeout.
Maximum **long polling** wait (`ReceiveMessageWaitTimeSeconds`). It cuts empty responses and cost compared with short polling.
Default and maximum message retention. A **dead-letter queue** catches messages after `maxReceiveCount` failed receives; **DLQ redrive** moves them back after a fix.
Maximum delivery delay, set per queue (**delay queue**) or per message (**message timer**, standard queues only). Longer delays need EventBridge Scheduler.
Maximum SQS message size (older questions may still say 256 KB). Larger payloads, up to 2 GB, use the **SQS Extended Client Library**, which stores the body in S3.

traps: Several consumers polling **one** SQS queue split the messages between them; none gets every message.
SQS deletes a message once it's processed, so it can't replay data to a second app; that's a Kinesis use case.
SQS has no message priority attribute; use separate queues for priority tiers.
Raising the visibility timeout to the longest possible job delays retries when a worker crashes.
Setting the **visibility timeout** to delay new messages is wrong; a **delay queue** hides messages before their first receive.
A delay of hours or days can't be done with SQS delays (15 min max); use EventBridge Scheduler.
SNS doesn't hold messages for a subscriber that is down for maintenance; put an SQS queue behind each subscription.
Moving a JMS/OpenWire or AMQP app to SQS means code changes, even with the SQS Java Messaging Library; Amazon MQ keeps the protocol.
